readiness.reason: Two verified static security blockers remain: F-001 (authenticated path traversal write/delete of arbitrary .json) and F-002 (spoofable or shared rate-limit key that breaks login, refresh and verify protection). No runtime tests exist.

F-001.reason: utils/playlist.rs:43-65 and 148-156 join unvalidated date parts. Role::User is allowed on save and delete, and import.rs:35-39 has the same pattern.

F-002.reason: main.rs:168-174 puts rate_limit outermost and main.rs:185 has no ConnectInfo. The key is spoofable via X-Forwarded-For or a constant 127.0.0.1, and the UserMeta bypass in governor.rs:42 never fires.

F-003.reason: Supervisor/reliability issue outside my security scope; I did not read run_channel.

F-004.reason: Control-flow race outside my scope; I did not review control.rs.

F-008.reason: I checked only that the updater trust boundary is sound (token auth, Docker socket only on Watchtower). The on-air guard is a reliability matter.

F-017.reason: auth.rs:462-470 leaves the 6-digit code valid after a wrong attempt, with no counter. Rate-limit bypass (F-002) makes brute force of the 5-minute window practical once the password is known.

F-018.reason: playout_config.rs:263-270 allows ChannelAdmin and stream_url is saved unvalidated (:461). engine/src/output/encoded.rs:445 opens it raw with a custom muxer, so ffmpeg can write a local path.

F-019.reason: logging.rs:759,796-802 logs the full URI including the access, key and uuid query secrets to the console target.

F-020.reason: routes/file.rs:372-385 writes env::temp_dir().join(user-supplied name), a predictable name in a shared dir. An import error skips cleanup, so the file is left behind.

F-021.reason: Database init, not reviewed beyond reading init.rs:27-50.

F-026.reason: Dockerfile user and healthcheck not reviewed. The compose file shows no hardening, but that is outside my scope.

F-027.reason: docker-compose.yml:43 uses untagged nickfedor/watchtower with the Docker socket mounted at :48, which is a supply-chain trust risk. It is opt-in via the updater profile, so I rate it low.

F-032.reason: Allowing Role::User to operate schedules is consistent with the role model used across routes (logo.rs:134-138, playlist routes). That is a policy choice; the duplicate-trigger reliability concern belongs to the schedule reviewers.

F-033.reason: SSE broadcaster performance, not reviewed. SSE auth (sse/routes.rs:88-103) is gated by a UUID bound to a user.

F-034.reason: auth.rs:87-98 embeds role and channels in the JWT, and user.rs update_user revokes no sessions or refresh families. Exposure is bounded to the 45-minute access lifetime plus any live refresh token.

F-035.reason: api/routes/setup.rs:33-47 is unauthenticated until setup completes, and docker-compose.yml:29 publishes 8787 on all interfaces. It is serialised and guarded, so this is first-run only and LOW.
